title: Perturbation campaign — OWL report (AWQ / GPTQ, int4-int8)
content:
Purpose:
This note summarizes the perturbation campaign we ran on the OWL promptset bank to measure practical quality deltas when applying AWQ- and GPTQ-style quantization at int4 and int8. The goal is to produce slice-level guidance for onboarding open models into Redwood’s serving runtime and for rollout policies (when to fall back to higher-precision variants).

High-level summary (TL;DR):
- AWQ-int4 shows the largest cost win but has a nonuniform degradation profile: predictable for short chit-chat and retrieval-style QA, but sharp regressions on long-context reasoning and chain-of-thought math.
- GPTQ-int4 is more conservative: fewer catastrophic failure modes, but still visible hallucination increases on safety-sensitive and multi-step instruction slices.
- int8 (both AWQ/int8 and GPTQ/int8) is broadly acceptable across most slices; marginal delta vs fp16 is often <0.4% for top-line EM/rouge metrics, but we see subtle calibration changes.
- Recommendation: gate AWQ-int4 behind per-route eval thresholds (slice-aware); default to GPTQ-int4 for mid-tier routes; use int8 as safe fallback for enterprise SLA routes.

Experiment matrix (condensed):
- Model base: open-model-x-13b (fp16 baseline)
- Variants: AWQ-int4, GPTQ-int4, AWQ-int8, GPTQ-int8
- Prompt bank: OWL promptset v3 (~3.2k prompts grouped into 42 slices)
- Sampling: deterministic (greedy) for exact-match tasks; nucleus sampling (p=0.9) for creative tasks to emulate product defaults
- Metrics: exact match (EM) for structured QA, Rouge-L for summarization tasks, BLEU for code-generation snippet matching, hallucination rate (human-annotated on a 5% sample), token-logprob shift, calibration (expected calibration error on confidence proxies)
- N per slice: 50–200 depending on slice cardinality; we used stratified sampling to keep rare slices represented

Promptset composition notes:
- OWL v3 includes: 1) instruction-following tasks (single-step), 2) multi-step planning/reasoning, 3) math (symbolic and word problems), 4) code generation (short snippets plus docstring tests), 5) long-document summarization (context windows up to 16k), 6) retrieval-style KB-QA, 7) multilingual (EN/ES/FR/DE/JA snippets), 8) safety-sensitive prompts (policy edge cases), 9) conversational chit-chat.

Slice definitions we tracked (representative):
- MULTI_STEP: problems requiring >2 reasoning steps (chain-of-thought)
- LONG_CONTEXT: summarization or QA with >8k tokens of context
- MATH_INT: arithmetic and symbolic reasoning
- CODE_SNIPPET: short functions with unit-test style check
- KB_QA: retrieval-anchored factual Q&A (ground-truth exists in KB)
- SAFETY_EDGE: ambiguous toxicity/policy edge cases
- MULTILINGUAL: non-English prompts or code-switching
- CHITCHAT: short conversational replies

Key quantitative findings (select slices; deltas relative to fp16 baseline):
- MULTI_STEP:
  - AWQ-int4: EM -9.6 pts, hallucination +12.4%
  - GPTQ-int4: EM -4.1 pts, hallucination +5.3%
  - AWQ-int8: EM -1.3 pts, hallucination +2.1%
  - GPTQ-int8: EM -0.9 pts, hallucination +1.8%

- LONG_CONTEXT:
  - AWQ-int4: Rouge-L -7.2 pts, token-logprob shift -0.42
  - GPTQ-int4: Rouge-L -3.5 pts, token-logprob shift -0.19
  - int8 variants: <=1.0 pt delta on rouge-L

- MATH_INT:
  - AWQ-int4: exact-solution drop -11.4 pts, incorrect-but-plausible answers rose significantly
  - GPTQ-int4: -5.9 pts

- CODE_SNIPPET:
  - AWQ-int4: unit-test pass rate -6.1 pts
  - GPTQ-int4: -2.2 pts
  - int8: within 1 pt of baseline

- KB_QA:
  - AWQ-int4: small EM drop (-2.8 pts) but higher wrong-assertion rate (model confidently states incorrect facts)
  - GPTQ-int4: negligible EM change, small calibration shift

- SAFETY_EDGE:
  - AWQ-int4: toxic-flag false negatives increased (human-annotated) by ~3.2% absolute — worrying for moderation-sensitive routes
  - GPTQ-int4: +1.0% absolute

- CHITCHAT / MULTILINGUAL: generally robust across quantizations; AWQ-int4 shows occasional non-sequitur replies for low-resource language prompts.

Observations / patterns we detected:
- AWQ’s weight compression exposes certain attention-kernel sensitivities for long-range dependencies; those propagate into chain-of-thought collapse and hallucination spikes.
- GPTQ’s heuristics tend to preserve important heads/kv-layouts leading to better multi-step stability at the cost of slightly higher memory/latency than AWQ-int4.
- int8 is a pragmatic sweet spot for most customer-facing routes where quality-corruption risk must be minimized.
- Token-logprob shifts correlate moderately with downstream hallucination; we can use an automated proxy (delta-logprob per token normalized by length) as a lightweight gate during rollout.

Actionable recommendations (immediate):
1) Rollout policy by slice:
   - enterprise-productivity routes + safety-sensitive: restrict to int8 (AWQ/GPTQ-int8 acceptable) until human verification step added.
   - low-risk consumer routes: trial AWQ-int4 with canary on 5% traffic for the first 72h and automatic rollback if slice-specific EM/hallucination thresholds exceeded.
   - developer preview / sandbox: allow AWQ-int4 as opt-in for cost-savings.
2) Add slice-aware monitoring hooks in Redwood Console: per-route slice breakdowns (_MULTI_STEP, LONG_CONTEXT, SAFETY_EDGE_) and automated alerts when hallucination proxy increases >5% over baseline.
3) Extend promptset with adversarial perturbations focused on long-context reasoning and numeric grounding (we added ~300 targeted perturbations; recommend expanding to 1k).
4) Implement a delta-logprob gate: if normalized token-logprob shifts beyond calibrated threshold, fallback to int8 or fp16.
5) For AWQ-int4, prioritize a small per-layer re-quantize pass for attention-kernel-critical layers (engineering ticket below).

Engineering/ops tickets (next work items):
- APPL-1324: implement per-slice rollout gating and canary automation (linked)
- APPL-1329: delta-logprob metric instrumentation & dashboard in Console
- APPL-1337: AWQ layer re-quantize experiment infra and micro-benchmarks
- APPL-1348: expand OWL adversarial prompt bank (+1k long-context/math probes)

Open questions / caveats:
- Our human annotation sample for hallucination was 5% by budget; some rare slices may be underpowered. Need larger human eval for MULTI_STEP and SAFETY_EDGE to firm thresholds.
- Results are on model-x-13b only; architecture-specific behavior may differ. We should run a 3-model sweep before company-wide policy.
- Latency/throughput tradeoffs: AWQ-int4 gives better token throughput in our local runtime but interacts with KV-cache eviction heuristics—need SRE bench to validate production P99.

Notes to reviewers:
- I purposefully kept the OWL prompt identifiers stable so these numbers can be cross-checked against the raw CSVs in the experiment S3 bucket (see PR#4567).
- If product owners prefer conservative policy language, escalate to "int8 default for SLA routes" as the primary recommendation.

Appendix (quick methodology checklist):
- seed: deterministic for EM tasks; seed range for stochastic tasks documented in PR
- de-dup: removed near-duplicate prompts across slices to avoid over-weighting
- human-review: 5% random sample stratified by slice; annotation schema attached to PR

Next steps (two-week plan):
- Week 1: Instrument delta-logprob gating and add initial slice dashboards (APPL-1329); start larger human eval on MULTI_STEP (budget request submitted).
- Week 2: Canary AWQ-int4 on non-SLA consumer route with automated rollback; run small AWQ layer re-quantize experiment and record unit test pass rates.

-- end of report --

Draft notes (internal):
- We should consider a short customer-facing one-pager summarizing cost/quality tradeoffs for AWQ vs GPTQ (keeping numbers high level).
- Asha suggested adding a "QA checklist" for solutions eng when enabling low-precision models for customers—agree, file a ticket after review.
